original_test_intent: Demonstrate that the intended Delta PSU can be moved through the approved firmware upgrade and downgrade path by the platform's Redfish update mechanism while the host is powered off, and that each activated target version is correctly reported without losing PSU health or system power redundancy.
original_method: Select the unique row; identify SUT/BMC/PSU bay, model, serial, current version and redundant feed; obtain the approved Delta SOP and paired signed upgrade/downgrade images; verify compatibility, hashes and activation/recovery requirements; drain workloads and power off the host through the approved method while retaining management/recovery access; execute one approved Redfish update direction; wait for its terminal task state without interruption; activate as documented and verify inventory/health; repeat the reverse direction only after separate approval and a healthy checkpoint; restore the required final version and power state.
manual_activity: An operator supplies and approves the Delta SOP, images, exact PSU/redundancy/power plan and each update direction; the agent may submit and monitor the specified Redfish task only after approval.
required_inputs: SUT, BMC and exact PSU bay/model/PN/serial/current firmware with feed/redundancy map
Delta PSU Update Instruction revision and supported Redfish endpoint/task schema
Approved upgrade and downgrade images, versions, hashes/signatures and compatibility matrix
Activation/reset/AC requirements, final desired version, maintenance window and independent power/recovery path
safety_requirements: Drain the host and prove the documented powered-off state before each flash
Prove the image matches the exact PSU target and preserve one healthy power/recovery path
Require explicit approval separately for upgrade, downgrade and any activation cycle
Do not interrupt, parallelize or automatically retry a firmware task
Stop on identity/hash/compatibility mismatch, loss of redundancy/access, failed/indeterminate task, PSU fault or unexpected power/thermal event
agent_execution_scope: Collect pre-flash inventory, image metadata and power/redundancy evidence
Submit only the approved Redfish payload to the mapped PSU and monitor its task to a defined terminal state
Collect activated version, health, SEL/power and final-state evidence after each direction
Do not invent an endpoint, select an image, authorize a flash/cycle, retry a failure or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve target PSU and the ordered upgrade/downgrade source/target/final versions
Approve images, signatures, compatibility, exact Redfish payload and task completion/activation oracle
Approve power-off/redundancy/maintenance and rollback/reflash/vendor recovery plan
Review each direction and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The prose correctly avoids fabricating a Redfish URI and retains the Delta SOP, but the source title requires both upgrade and downgrade while image pairing, target mapping, activation and final restoration remain unspecified.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the exact Delta-SOP Redfish request for the verified PSU/image/direction after approval; preserve HTTP/task progress and do not issue a second request until the first task, activation and health checks are conclusively complete.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Host power-off, Delta SOP, Redfish mechanism, both upgrade/downgrade title coverage, firmware-version check and 60/60-minute estimate remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Treat each direction as an independently approved transaction with immutable target/image metadata, task-state monitoring, activation proof, PSU health/redundancy checkpoint and explicit final-version restoration.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds per-bay identity, signed image compatibility, directional checkpoints, task/activation semantics, redundancy, final state and vendor recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A successful upload or task alone does not prove that the intended PSU activated the target version, that downgrade is supported or that redundancy remains healthy.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: A PSU flash can make a module unavailable, remove redundancy or power the SUT down; some implementations stage firmware until a PSU/BMC/AC event that must not be guessed.

project_override_considerations: If policy prohibits downgrade or supports only a single powered module at a time, engineering must define the approved alternate coverage or exception without deleting the title requirement. A Redfish UpdateService URI must be supplied by the platform SOP, not inferred from another BMC.
expected_evidence: Approved SOP and immutable upgrade/downgrade image version/hash/signature records
Per-direction secret-redacted Redfish request metadata, HTTP/task timeline and terminal state
Pre/staged/active/post firmware inventory and PSU health/redundancy
SEL/power/thermal/host logs, final restored version/power state and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The title requires upgrade and downgrade, and the generic update procedure can encompass both directions under the cited Delta SOP. Missing target versions and mechanics are project inputs rather than contradictory source statements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The intended Delta PSU firmware lifecycle and Redfish mechanism are identifiable. SOP, images, target mapping and recovery are expected vendor/project prerequisites, so the case remains conditionally executable rather than intrinsically blocked.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2231 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00013-V001: approve the SUT/BMC and exact Delta PSU bay/model/PN/serial/feed/redundancy mapping; Delta SOP revision and exact Redfish endpoint/payload/task/activation semantics; ordered upgrade, downgrade and final versions with signed image names/hashes/compatibility; host-off and maintenance plan, terminal timeout, health oracle, required reset/AC action, aborts and rollback/reflash/vendor recovery.

review_improvement: Preserves both upgrade and downgrade coverage while converting an underspecified critical flash into separately authorized, identity-bound, observable and recoverable transactions.
independent_technical_reasoning: PSU firmware is part of the active power-delivery chain, so flashing the wrong bay or an incompatible image can remove redundancy even when the host is nominally off. Redfish provides transport and task status, but it does not by itself prove the module activated the intended version or recovered healthy. Upgrade and downgrade must therefore be distinct checkpoints with immutable image/target identity and a known final state. A failed or indeterminate task is specifically unsafe to retry automatically because the module may already be partially programmed.
